This pathway leads from a first-year undergraduate (L1) level (calculus, linear algebra, some programming) to the level required to start the MilaDy internship: reading a paper on generative models under physical constraints, writing and training a conditional flow matching model, and assessing a generated MHD field against physical criteria. It comprises **eight modules**, about **215 hours** of work and **121 exercises with solutions**.

::: note
[About]{.tag}
These modules are independent notes. They are not an official course of ENPC, LISN or Université Paris-Saclay. Each module lists its sources; facts about recent research come from verified fact bases (the `specs/sources/` folder of the repository).
:::

## The eight modules {#modules}

| Module | Level | Duration | Exercises | What it brings to the internship |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1. Vector calculus and Fourier analysis](p1-calcul-vectoriel/index.html) | L1 → L2 | 20 h | 15 | divergence, curl, potentials, FFT, Leray projection |
| [2. Fluid mechanics and turbulence](p2-mecanique-fluides/index.html) | L2 → M1 | 25 h | 15 | Navier–Stokes, energy budgets, spectra, pseudo-spectral methods |
| [3. Electromagnetism, MHD and the dynamo effect](p3-mhd-dynamo/index.html) | L2 → M2 | 30 h | 14 | induction equation, $Rm$, laboratory dynamos, reversals |
| [4. Dynamical systems and invariant measures](p4-systemes-dynamiques/index.html) | L2 → M2 | 25 h | 15 | bifurcations, chaos, stationarity identities, Rice formula |
| [5. Probability, statistics and optimal transport](p5-probabilites-transport/index.html) | L2 → M1 | 25 h | 15 | pushforward measure, KL and I-projection, distances between distributions, SDEs |
| [6. Deep learning for physics](p6-apprentissage-profond/index.html) | L3 → M2 | 30 h | 16 | neural networks, POD and autoencoders, equivariance, PINNs and operators |
| [7. Generative models: diffusion and flow matching](p7-modeles-generatifs/index.html) | M1 → M2 | 30 h | 16 | diffusion, score, flow matching, conditioning, FunDiff |
| [8. Generative models under physical constraints](p8-contraintes-physiques/index.html) | M2 → research | 30 h | 15 | taxonomy of constraints, projections, penalties, distributional constraints |

## In what order {#ordre}

Modules 1 to 3 form the **physics** branch, modules 5 to 8 the **learning** branch; module 4 links the two, because it explains why a stationary turbulent state is described by an invariant probability distribution.

- **Physics**: 1 → 2 → 3. Module 3 uses the potentials and the projection from module 1, and the energy budgets from module 2.
- **Bridge**: 4, after 2 and 5. It is used for reversals (module 3) and for distributional constraints (module 8).
- **Learning**: 5 → 6 → 7 → 8. Module 7 requires the pushforward measure and the continuity equation from module 5; module 8 requires all the others.

A linear reading order that respects these dependencies is 1, 2, 5, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8.

## A possible schedule {#calendrier}

To start the internship in spring 2027, at a pace of about 15 hours per week:

| Weeks | Modules | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | 1 | be able to project a periodic field onto divergence-free fields |
| 3–4 | 2 | have run a 2D pseudo-spectral solver and checked its energy budget |
| 5–6 | 5 | be able to compute an I-projection and an energy distance |
| 7–8 | 3 | be able to explain the threshold of a kinematic dynamo and the VKS reversals |
| 9–10 | 4 | be able to check a stationarity identity and the Rice formula on a simple model |
| 11–12 | 6 | have compared POD and an autoencoder on fields |
| 13–14 | 7 | have trained a conditional flow matching model |
| 15 | 8 | have read the five references of the internship offer and reproduced an experiment from the [report](../rapport/index.html) |

## How to work through a module {#methode}

Each module follows the same structure: objectives, prerequisites, work plan (sessions, durations, levels from 1 to 3 that never go back down), chapters with definitions, theorems and proofs, executed Python code, graded exercises ★ / ★★ / ★★★ with solutions, connection to the internship, further reading and sources.

- Read a chapter, then do the exercises listed in its work plan before reading the solution.
- Run each code block and change a parameter: every block runs in under 30 seconds on a laptop.
- Keep one page of formulas per module; module 8 assumes you can retrieve them quickly.
- The [interactive diagrams](../interactifs/index.html) illustrate five key notions: flow matching, Leray projection, distributional constraint, reversals and the ABC dynamo.
